text:
If you've got outdoor plans today, front-load them: mornings are the calm before a genuinely wet stretch moves in. We're starting clear and mild, but showers and thunderstorms build in by early afternoon, with a high near 85. The Euro is much wetter than the American model here (near 100% chance versus 60%) and even the sunnier read keeps the sky unsettled, so I'd trust the forecasters' own call of 80% and plan around scattered downpours from midday on, some potentially heavy.

Tonight is when it gets serious: rain becomes steady and widespread, 90% coverage, with isolated flash flooding possible if storms stall over the same spot, mainly south of us. Wednesday stays cloudy and showery with a high only near 77, and the wet pattern holds into Wednesday night. On the lake, winds stay light out of the south early, but afternoon storms mean you want to be off the broad waters well before that early-afternoon window, and the air's just moderate today from lingering smoke, not a big deal for most. Bottom line: enjoy the morning, but plan any lake time or long outdoor stretch before 1pm, because the rest of the day through Wednesday is a wash.
